Control Theory Toolbox · Bode, Nyquist, Root Locus, Routh–Hurwitz

Continuous-time SISO transfer functions with real polynomial coefficients, highest power first. Frequency is in rad/s. This is a numerical analysis workspace, not a certified stability tool.

Frequency response · stability margins, bandwidth, resonant peak

Uses the numerator, denominator and gain above. Gain/phase crossovers are bracketed on a log-ω grid over 0.01–1000 rad/s and refined by bisection with unwrapped phase; bandwidth and Mr use the unity-feedback closed loop T = KG/(1+KG). Crossings outside the range are reported as not found (infinite margin). Choose Bode mode above to mark the crossovers on the plot.

🎨 Appearance · colors and styles









Styles apply to equation plots and table charts. Settings are saved in your project.



        

        
Plot y=f(x) in 2D; plot z=f(x,y) alone or pair it with y=f(x) to highlight a curve in 3D. Supported: polynomials, rational functions, trig, logs, powers, abs, min/max, and if(condition, true, false).

        
Supported functions and interactions
2D: y=x^2, y=1/(x-1), y=sin(3x), y=exp(-x^2), or y=if(x<0,-x,x). Separate curves by newline. 3D: z=sin(sqrt(x^2+y^2)), z=x^2-y^2, or the paired lines y=x×x and z=sin(x×y). Paired equations draw the surface and highlight its constrained 3D curve (x, x², sin(x³)). A single y=f(x) is drawn as a curve on the z=0 plane. Rotate by dragging, use Pan 3D or Shift + drag to move the view, and scroll to zoom toward the pointer. Click Axes & grid to set X/Y/Z bounds and grid spacing. Multiple surfaces can be entered on separate lines as z=..., z2=... and z3=.... Radian trig notation is used for graphs.

Fractions and parentheses: For a denominator of x − 1, type x/(x-1). For an exponent of −½, type ^(-1/2) or ^-1/2. This prevents ambiguous grouping.

Math notation guide

  
Type the notation below in the editor. The preview typesets it immediately, then Enter adds it to your notebook.

  

    
x^2, x_1, x_1^2
Powers and subscripts

    
a/b, a/(b+c)
Stacked fractions and grouped denominators

    
x^(-1/2), x^-1/2
Fractional and negative exponents

    
sqrt(x), root(3,x)
Square and nth roots

    
pi, alpha, theta, infty
Greek letters and infinity

    
sin(x), cos(x), log(x)
Trigonometric and logarithmic functions

    
sum(i=1,n,i^2)
Sum with limits and expression

    
int(0,1,x^2,x)
Definite integral: lower, upper, function, variable

    
lim(x->0,sin(x)/x)
Limit with approach expression

    
<=, >=, !=, +-, ->
≤, ≥, ≠, ±, →

    
abs(x), |x|, vec(v)
Absolute value and vector accent

    
2x, (a+b)(c+d)
Implicit multiplication

    
(x-1)^2, x^2=1, x^2=-1
Execute: expand algebra or solve for real/complex roots

    
diff(x^3,x), pdiff(f,x)
Ordinary and partial derivatives

    
diffn(f,x,2), grad(f)
Higher derivatives and vector calculus

    
matrix([a,b],[c,d])
2×2 matrix (each bracket is a row)

    
array([a,b],[c,d])
Array without surrounding brackets

    
pmatrix([1,2],[3,4])
Matrix with round brackets

    
det([a,b],[c,d])
Matrix determinant with vertical bars

    
cases([x,x>=0],[-x,x<0])
Piecewise expression

    
vector(x,y,z), binom(n,k)
Column vector and binomial coefficient

    
iint(D,f,x,y), oint(C,F,x)
Double and contour integrals

    
norm(v), dot(u,v), cross(u,v)
Vector norms, scalar and cross products

    
set(a,b,c), union(A,B)
Sets and operations

    
expect(X), variance(X), prob(A)
Probability and statistics

  
Word: Use Copy for Word to copy formatted MathML (rich HTML) and paste into Word. For guaranteed editable native Word equations, download the Word .docx file. Python: Generated SymPy is symbolic code, not a numerical solver; some advanced notation requires mathematical conventions not inferred from the text.
Symbolic execution: Select an operation, specify the variable, and choose Execute or Ctrl + Enter. Auto expands expressions and solves equalities. Symbolic results can be saved or exported as editable Word equations. Some advanced operations need Python/SymPy, and rational expressions retain the original domain restrictions.
Important: x/x-1 is parsed as (x/x)-1, not x/(x-1). Add parentheses to express your intended grouping. Numerical superscript fractions like x^-1/2 are recognized as x^(-1/2).
